audit.why: Lane difficulty reads as a poke war Jayce wins early: Emerald+ 53.04% over 807 games, and the content/full charts agree Jayce owns Levels 2-3 and the first-item window. Mel is 950-range artillery with a 1000-range root; the difficulty genuinely sits in whether the player holds the orb through Rebuttal.

audit.whatIsWrong: `early` calls Rebuttal 'her ultimate' and `whys[4]` says 'Her R is just your stance-swap' — a line describing Jayce's own R attached to Mel.
audit.why: Riot's kit: Rebuttal is Mel's W (38/35/33/29/26s), a barrier that reflects projectiles, blocks damage and grants move speed. Her ultimate is Golden Eclipse, 120/100/80s, 25000 range, striking every Overwhelm-marked enemy anywhere on the map. Calling the W an ult tells the player a 38-second cooldown only comes up from Level 6, so they will poke freely at Levels 2-5 straight into a reflect that is already available. And Golden Eclipse being global means Level 6 is a real spike for her that the page never mentions at all.
audit.corrected: Rebuttal is her W at 38s rank 1 and is live from Level 2; Golden Eclipse is the 120s global execute at 6.

audit.whatIsWrong: `wants.you[1]` and `early` both put the Armor/MR shred on the swap to Hammer. The direction is backwards.
audit.why: Riot's Mercury Cannon/Mercury Hammer: from Hammer Stance the swap transforms into the Mercury Cannon and 'the first attack in this form reduces the target's Armor and Magic Resist'; from Cannon Stance the swap gives Mercury Hammer and its first attack 'deals additional magic damage'. So the shred is the first attack after swapping INTO Cannon. Mel builds no resistances and dies to magic-shred plus burst, so a player told to shred on the Hammer swap spends the wrong half of a 6-second toggle and lands zero shred on the all-in that needed it.
audit.corrected: The shred is the first attack after swapping into Mercury Cannon; the Hammer-form first hit is bonus magic damage instead.

audit.whatIsWrong: Solar Snare is never named in the content layer, and the full layer names it without saying what it does.
audit.why: Solar Snare is Mel's E at 1000 range on 11/10.5/10/9.5/9s — a projectile that roots at its centre with a surrounding slow-and-damage zone. It is the only hard CC she has and the only way she lands a full Radiant Volley plus Golden Eclipse on a Jayce who can kite with Hextech Capacitor. It is also the shortest of her meaningful cooldowns, which is what makes the trading rule concrete rather than vague.
audit.corrected: Named with its 11s rank-1 cooldown and its root-centre/slow-edge behaviour in the cooldown block and the dont.

audit.whatIsWrong: Full layer refers to Mel as 'he'/'his' in phases[4].why, breakdown.mid and dosFull.
audit.why: Mel is female; Riot's own ability text uses 'she' throughout. Misgendering on a live page reads as a page written by someone who has not played the matchup, which costs trust on every other claim.
audit.corrected: Corrected in the strings edited here; remaining instances flagged in notes.

edits.before: Mel is a newer artillery mage who wants to win the poke war from range, but your gate-Q out-ranges her Q outright once you have Acceleration Gate at Level 2. Take Shock Blast (Cannon Q) at Level 1, range-check her on the first wave, and from Level 2-3 punish every step-up: fire the accelerated orb through the gate, and if she walks in, swap to Hammer for the Armor/MR shred and chunk her. The one rule is her ultimate (Rebuttal) reflects projectiles — never throw a gate-Q into it or your own orb comes back and bursts you instead.
edits.after: Mel is an artillery mage who wants the poke war from range, but your gate-Q out-ranges Radiant Volley once Acceleration Gate lands at Level 2. Take Shock Blast at Level 1, then from 2-3 punish every step-up through the gate. Two rules. Rebuttal is her W, not her ult, so the 38-second reflect is live from Level 2 — hold the orb while the barrier is up. And the Armor/MR shred is the first attack after you swap into Mercury Cannon, not into Hammer, so open the commit with that attack.

edits.before: Land a swap-shred onto her Armor/MR, then To-the-Skies in for the Lightning Field + Thundering Blow burst
edits.after: Swap into Mercury Cannon so the first attack shreds her Armor/MR, then To-the-Skies into Thundering Blow

edits.before: Her Rebuttal reflects projectiles, so never fire a gate-Q into it — a reflected Shock Blast comes straight back and chunks you instead.
edits.after: Rebuttal (W, 38s at rank 1) reflects projectiles, so never fire a gate-Q into the barrier — your own Shock Blast comes back at you.

edits.before: Her R is just your stance-swap with no spike at 6, but firing a gate-Q into Rebuttal hands her the trade — so the orb timing is the swing skill of this lane.
edits.after: Golden Eclipse is a 120s global execute off her Overwhelm stacks, and your R is only the stance-swap — so 6 is her spike, not yours, and orb timing decides it.

edits.before: - Mel Solar Snare: matchup-defining — Her root / slow zone — sets up her combo. Dodge it. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Mel Solar Snare: 11s at rank 1, roots at the centre — the only CC that stops your kite. - Mel Rebuttal: 38s at rank 1 and it reflects Shock Blast — poke the moment the barrier drops. - Thundering Blow: 20s, your one commit.

edits.before: Burning it for tiny value leaves you naked for its full cooldown.
edits.after: Rebuttal reflects the orb; wait out its 38 seconds instead.

edits.before: Form-swapping IS the ult — six abilities against his four. Reassess every all-in at 6 — Mel's ultimate changes the math too.
edits.after: Form-swapping IS your ult, so 6 adds nothing. Golden Eclipse does: a 120s global execute off her Overwhelm stacks reaches you anywhere.
